name: Persuasive Writing Common Pitfalls
description: This module lists frequently observed mistakes, bugs, and anti-patterns seen in everyday persuasive writing work, so they can be recognized and avoided during typical persuasive writing tasks.
content:
This module lists frequently observed mistakes, bugs, and anti-patterns seen in everyday persuasive writing work, so they can be recognized and avoided during typical persuasive writing tasks.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. Prefer explicit, readable persuasive writing solutions over clever ones that are hard to verify.
2. Keep persuasive writing changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.
3. When multiple persuasive writing strategies are viable, name the trade-off explicitly rather than silently picking one.
4. Validate persuasive writing outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.
5. Keep persuasive writing outputs reproducible: fix seeds, record versions, and avoid hidden non-determinism where it matters.
6. Re-check edge cases relevant to persuasive writing (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.
7. Check that persuasive writing terminology is used consistently throughout, matching existing conventions in the surrounding context.
8. Before starting persuasive writing work, confirm the scope and constraints so the approach matches the actual requirement.
9. State assumptions about persuasive writing explicitly before proceeding, rather than leaving them implicit.
10. Document any non-obvious persuasive writing decision with a short rationale so future readers understand the 'why', not just the 'what'.
11. When persuasive writing decisions are ambiguous, favor the option that is easiest to reverse or extend later.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not treat a single passing example as full verification of persuasive writing correctness.
- Do not skip documenting persuasive writing assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.
- Avoid introducing new persuasive writing abstractions before there is a second concrete use case that needs them.

CLOSING NOTE
Revisit these persuasive writing guidelines if the task's constraints change significantly during the work.
